title: Vanishing & Exploding Gradients — Preserve Scale Statistically
key_insight: Xavier and He initialization choose weight variance from the number of incoming or outgoing connections. Their assumptions match different activation families.
body:
## Preserve Scale Statistically

No single connection is alarming, yet millions of random connections collectively change variance from layer to layer.

Xavier and He initialization choose weight variance from the number of incoming or outgoing connections. Their assumptions match different activation families.

Recurrent networks repeatedly reuse the same transformation, making scale problems especially severe. Gated cells and orthogonal starting matrices help preserve information over longer sequences.
common_mistakes: Vanishing gradients make every update infinitely large.
Gradient clipping creates new labels for the dataset.
Depth can never affect backward signal scale.
mini_exercise: Sketch the situation in “Preserve Scale Statistically” as three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Unhealthy gradient scale prevents early layers from learning and can make training numerically unstable.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “Preserve Scale Statistically” situation, explain Vanishing & Exploding Gradients without assuming the listener knows deep learning.
